texts.preamble: Devendra Ku. Agrawal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 February, 2022 Author: Virender Singh Bench: Virender Singh 1 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh : Jabalpur Criminal Revision No.3568/2021 (Devendra Ku. Agarwal Vs. State of M.P Jabalpur, dated : 24-02-2022 Shri Vijay Nayak, counsel for the petitio Shri Chandrapal Singh Parma, Public Prose respondent No.1-State. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that now the petitioner has surrendered and he is in jail.
texts.facts: 2. Also heard on I.A.No.23230/2021 which is the first application under Section 397(1) of CrPC for suspension of sentence of the petitioner. 3. By way of present revision under Section 397/401 of CrPC, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and order dated 30.10.2021 passed in CRA No.134/2015 by the Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Hoshangabad, District Hoshangabad whereby the judgment dated 23.07.2015 passed in Criminal Case No.1704/2010 by JMFC, Hoshangabad, District Hoshangabad has been upheld. 4. As informed by the ld. counsel for the petitioner, the fine amount has been deposited.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that now the petitioner has surrendered and he is in jail. Relying on the statement of learned counsel for the petitioner, it is presumed that the petitioner is in jail. 5. The grounds taken by the ld. counsel for the petitioner are that no standard for "Namkeen Sev" (a salted snack) has been prescribed in the Act and the FSL report does not state as to how the sample was adulterated or sub-standard. There is no mention in the FSL report of existence of presence of starch in the sample. The FSL report also does not say that the sample was injurious to health or was not fit for human consumption, therefore, the conviction recorded by both the Courts below is contrary to law. 6. The other grounds taken by the ld. counsel for the petitioner are that provision of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act has not been complied with. The petitioner has been deprived from his valuable rights. The compliance of the provision was mandatory and its non-compliance is fatal to the prosecution case. Public Analyst has not been examined before the trial Court and lastly, it is submitted that witness of seizure has turned hostile, therefore, there are fair chances of the petitioner for his acquittal. The revision would take time to be heard finally. The petitioner is ready to furnish adequate surety and to abide by all the terms and conditions as may be imposed by the Court, therefore, prayer is made to suspend the custodial sentence of the petitioner. 7. Learned counsel for the petitioner referred to the judgment of this Court rendered in the case of Kanwarlal Vs State of M.P. reported in 2002 (4) M.P.H.T. 402 wherein this Court has held that when the Public Analyst's report does not say that Namkeen Sev was not upto the standard as prescribed for gram-flour (Besan) and foreign matter i.e. starch was present in it, the accused is entitled for acquittal. 8. While opposing the prayer, the ld. Public Prosecutor for the State has referred to the paragraphs 26, 27 and 28 of the judgment of the trial Court and submitted that trial Court has considered the grounds raised by the petitioner before this Court and has discarded them rightly. The report is as under : Sl. Quality Characteristics Name of Result Prescribed Standards No. Method of as per test used (a) Item A ...... (b) As per label declaration for proprietory foods. Test for Added Colour Q.G.H.S Negative method 2. Test for salt ---"--- Positive 3. Test for Khesaridal ---"--- Positive Powder 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that while dismissing the first application for suspension of sentence, this Court has recorded its findings on the issue of adulteration as well as issue of exercising the right conferred under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, therefore, this Court has now become functus officio and cannot hear this case finally and let the case be adjourned.
